reasoning: The domain has 600 points and the metered budget is 120 credits, so no brute-force sweep of the domain is affordable (range 1 600 costs 600 and would be refused). I therefore treated identification of f, not enumeration of f, as the problem. Four samples (n=1..4) determine an order-2 linear recurrence over F_5003: f(1)=43, f(2)=271, f(n)=12*f(n-1)+4968*f(n-2) mod 5003, with 4968 = -35 mod 5003. I then bought 14 further metered observations purely as out-of-sample tests of that model: n=5,6,7,8 and n=37,99,150,233,301,388,450,512,577,600, the last being the domain endpoint. All 14 predictions matched exactly; under a false model the chance of that is on the order of 5003^-14. One evaluate call at n=600 confirmed that the verdict instrument agrees with the value instrument (f(600)=3078, holds=true). Under the identified model, f(n) != 4038 for every n in [1,600] (exhaustive over the full 600-point domain, computed offline in verify_nav0010.py, not a bounded search inside a larger space). The stronger structural fact is that the state (f(n),f(n+1)) is purely periodic with period 5002 and the orbit takes only 3151 distinct values, of which 4038 is not one -- so 4038 is unreachable for every n, not merely for n <= 600. Stated limitation, in the required words: my confirmation of the model is a bounded check, bounded to the 18 points actually observed. Because only 120 of 600 points are affordable, no seat in this condition can exclude a single planted off-model point by observation alone; that residual is why my confidence is 0.93 and not 1.0. Everything else -- the exhaustive [1,600] sweep and the orbit-membership argument -- is exact integer arithmetic mod a prime, no floating point anywhere.
route_taken: Spent 4 credits to fit an order-2 linear recurrence mod 5003, 14 credits on out-of-sample points spread across the whole domain (including the endpoint) to test that model rather than to enumerate the domain, and 1 evaluate call to cross-check the two instruments -- 19 credits total -- because enumerating [1,600] costs 600 and even the affordable 120-point prefix would have covered only a fifth of the domain while telling me nothing about the other 480 points, whereas identifying the generator settles all 600 at once.
what_would_resolve_it: The only residual risk is an adversarially planted single-point deviation from the recurrence, which is unobservable at this budget: closing it needs either the sealed generator specification, an assurance that f is generated by a single fixed rule over the whole domain, or a metered budget of at least 600 credits to sweep [1,600] exhaustively via range 1 600.
